AtomicFileWrite.swift:31: rename(2) drops the old destination's xattrs, ACLs and owner, which replaceItemAt used to keep. The mode is still preserved when permissions is nil, and no current caller seems to depend on the rest, but this is an unstated behavior change. Worth one sentence in the doc comment.

UpdateCheckerDownloadTests: quarantine_failure_throws is now in the instance suite, so it creates and deletes a downloads dir it never uses. Harmless, but it could be a static test if the suite grows.

performance: AtomicFileWrite.swift:67 now runs fsync on every write. That includes the best-effort DiskCache error-marker write (DiskCache.swift:165), each per-vendor cache write per refresh cycle, and ConfigLoader.save, which may run on the main actor from settings UI. It is probably cheap for such small files, but it is I/O the diff added. Send it to the performance lens to confirm that no MainActor call site pays for it.

scope/metadata: rename(2) drops the xattrs and ACLs of the replaced file, which FileManager.replaceItemAt used to preserve. This is low impact for app-owned files, but ~/.codex/auth.json belongs to the Codex CLI and gets rewritten when manage_oauth_refresh=true.

title: AtomicFileWrite now replaces a symlinked destination with a regular file, silently
evidence: Measured with a probe: with HEAD's replaceItemAt, a symlinked dest makes the write THROW (NSCocoaError 4) and the link and its target stay unchanged. With the new rename(2) at AtomicFileWrite.swift:31, the link itself is replaced by a regular file. The link target stays stale, and existingMode (:38) takes the target's mode through stat, which follows the link.
impact: Affects users who symlink ~/.codex/auth.json or config.toml from a dotfiles repo. Before, every write failed loudly; for auth.json with manage_oauth_refresh=true this already lost the rotated token. Now the write succeeds and the CLI reads the new file, but the symlink is broken without warning. Functionally this is not worse than HEAD, so I am not blocking. It is still an undocumented change in contract.
suggestion: Decide explicitly and pin it with a test. Either resolve dest with realpath and write into the target's directory (keeps the dotfile link), or detect the symlink with lstat and fail. Also note that replacing the file drops the old file's ACLs and xattrs, which replaceItemAt used to keep.
